newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says U.S. cannot dictate peace formula.
newsitem.headline: Israel says U.S. cannot dictate peace formula.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in remarks published on Wednesday that Israel was not an American "client state" and Washington could not dictate formulas for reviving Middle East peacemaking.

"There are no American client states here," Netanyahu told the Haaretz newspaper in an interview published after the White House announced that it was sending U.S. Middle Envoy envoy Dennis Ross to the region for high- level talks on advancing the peace process.

"The United States is a partner in efforts, not only on our part but on the part of Palestinians as well, to reach an agreed settlement and the key word is agreed. This must be accomplished through consultation and agreement and not by dictates," he said.

Diplomatic sources have said the United States is drafting an initiative to revive peacemaking -- stalled since March -- that includes an Israeli freeze on building new Jewish settlements in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

"The United States is prepared to do everything it can to ensure that the peace process continues on a sound and durable basis," White House spokesman Mike McCurry said. "In that spirit, the Ambassador Ross will be conveying some U.S. ideas."
Palestinians have conditioned a renewal of peace talks on an Israeli settlement freeze, something which Netanyahu rejects.
Ross's visit follows a flurry of diplomatic activity including talks in Amman on Tuesday between Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy and Jordan's King Hussein.
